A.explanation: This is only the upward area from $1.0\text{ s}$ to $1.5\text{ s}$, not the net displacement from X.

B.explanation: Net displacement is $5.00\text{ m}$ down minus $1.25\text{ m}$ up, giving $3.75\text{ m}$ from X.

C.explanation: This is only the downward area from $0$ to $1.0\text{ s}$ and ignores the $1.25\text{ m}$ rebound back upward.

D.explanation: This adds the two areas as $5.00 + 1.25$, which is total distance travelled, not displacement from X.

hints: Notice the velocity sign: positive to $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $1.0\text{ s}$ is motion away from X, while negative from $-5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $0$ is motion back toward X.
Recall displacement is the signed area under the velocity-time graph, so the $0$ to $1.0\text{ s}$ triangle and the $1.0\text{ s}$ to $1.5\text{ s}$ triangle have opposite signs.
Calculate the large downward triangle area and subtract the small upward triangle magnitude to get net distance from X.
walkthrough: Take downward as positive because the released ball gains positive velocity from $0$ to $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ between $0$ and $1.0\text{ s}$.
Displacement $0$ to $1.0\text{ s}$ is the triangle area: $s_1 = \frac{1}{2} \times 1.0\text{ s} \times 10\text{ m s}^{-1} = 5.00\text{ m}$ downward.
After the inelastic bounce at $1.0\text{ s}$ the velocity is $-5\text{ m s}^{-1}$, so motion is upward, and it returns to $0$ at $1.5\text{ s}$ at the top of the bounce.

Upward displacement $1.0\text{ s}$ to $1.5\text{ s}$ is the signed triangle area: $s_2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.50\text{ s} \times (-5\text{ m s}^{-1}) = -1.25\text{ m}$, meaning $1.25\text{ m}$ upward.
Net displacement from X is $s_1 + s_2 = 5.00 - 1.25 = 3.75\text{ m}$ downward. This is option B.
